title: AFCON (Q): Mali seize top spot in Group J; Cape Verde earn first points

 Andrew Olsson · Nov 13, 2026 Photo: Rwanda Football Federation Rwanda came just short of earning a result at group leaders Mali on Saturday, and earlier in the day it was Cape Verde who bounced back from a poor start in Group K action from 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying.
 Tied on six points with Rwanda heading into their clash at the Stade du 26 Mars in Bamako, Mali were widely expected to seize top spot. However, the Eagles were given all they could handle before Mamadou Camara's first national team goal gave Mali a thrilling 3-2 victory.

 Mali dominated the opening twenty minutes and pinned the visitors in their half. However, a shock development arrived in the 29th minute when a quick attack down the left flank resulted in Jojea Kwizera's finish from a cross by Elie Tatou Iradukunda.
 Just before halftime, Mali responded through Kamory Doumbia's close range strike but another American-based player responded for the visitors when Birmingham Legion defender Kavita nodded in from Rhode Island FC star Kwizera. 
 The back-and-forth battle continued on with Moussa Yeo's equalizer in the 63rd minute, before Camara headed in Daouda Guindo's excellent corner kick to give the hosts the edge.
 Earlier on Saturday, it was Cape Verde who emerged victorious by a 4-2 score over Liberia at home in a battle between teams who had lost each of their opening two fixtures.

 Talented PSV Eindhoven midfielder Ayoni Santos scored his first goal for Cape Verde to open the scoring inside five minutes. Liberia responded later in the first half but Dailon Livramento's goal capped off a double blow dealt to the Lone Star just before halftime.
 The difficulty of Liberia's qualifying campaign was summarized well by the substitution of goalkeeper Ashley Williams at halftime, for what appeared to be purely performance reasons rather than an injury. Cape Verde added one more goal in second half stoppage time before Liberia scored their second from a penalty kick.
 Mali lead the group on nine points with a perfect start, with Rwanda now three points back. Cape Verde are on three points in third and Liberia still have zero points. The same duels will take place again on November 17 with Rwanda and Liberia hosting their respective opponents.
